forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Wolverhampton pension fund issued only 80% of member benefit statements by legal deadline
news_drafts.lead: West Midlands Pension Fund was unable to issue annual benefit statements to all members by the statutory 31 August 2025 deadline, and has still not fully caught up a year later. As of August 2026, the fund had produced benefit statements for 80% of active members and 93% of deferred members, according to the fund's own audit findings report. The regulator was notified of the miss. The failure comes as the fund's net assets grew to £24.6 billion in the three months to June 2026, up £1.2 billion, and investment management costs fell to 0.41% of assets. The fund is also facing new regulatory requirements from April 2026 that will require retrospective review of member benefits, with implementation costs still to be quantified and work extending to 2028.

news_drafts.headline: Wolverhampton Council repaid £17m in loans to avoid proposed rate increases of up to 6.26% on LOBO facilities
news_drafts.lead: Wolverhampton Council rejected proposals to increase rates on three bank loans totaling £17m and chose instead to repay them in full. LOBO loans are bank loans where lenders can propose new terms on set dates. Between July 2025 and January 2026, a £7m Commerzbank loan came with a proposed rate of 6.19%, compared with its existing 3.60%; two £5m Dexia loans proposed 6.21% and 6.26%, against existing rates of 4.26% and 4.29%. According to the Treasury Management Annual Report, this refinancing required £17m in cash but protected the council from substantially higher day-to-day running costs.

findings.headline: Current assets in the pension fund fell 47% in the quarter, from £88.8m to £47.1m, with no explanation provided
findings.detail: The net assets statement shows current assets declining significantly from £88.8m at 31 March to £47.1m at 30 June, a reduction of £41.7m. The bulk annuity insurance buy-in policy also decreased from £85.3m to £82.2m. The accounts contain no explanation for either movement.
findings.matters: A sharp quarterly decline in liquid current assets may indicate cash flow timing or reflect working capital reductions that the council or a lender would need to understand, particularly if it signals liquidity pressures or changes in fund management
findings.figures: Current assets: £88.8m to £47.1m (-£41.7m, -47%); bulk annuity policy: £85.3m to £82.2m (-£3.1m)

findings.headline: Pension fund grew by £1.267bn in Q1 2026-27 with net investment returns of £1.359bn
findings.detail: The fund's assets increased from £23.368bn at 31 March 2026 to £24.636bn at 30 June 2026, a 5.4% quarterly gain. Investment returns totalled £1.359bn, comprising £1.336bn of positive changes in investment values, £23.2m investment income, and offset by £0.1m of other adjustments. Pooled investment vehicles increased by £1.183bn and overseas equities rose by £140.2m, while direct property holdings declined by £13.5m.
findings.matters: A growing and well-performing pension fund reduces the likelihood of the council needing to increase contributions from its budget to cover shortfalls, strengthening the council's overall financial position and borrowing capacity
findings.figures: Fund grew from £23.368bn to £24.636bn (increase £1.267bn); net investment return £1.359bn; investment value gains £1.336bn
findings.quote: Net Increase in the Fund During the Period 1,267.1

findings.headline: SCAPE factor change is halting pension casework and expected to worsen performance in coming months.
findings.detail: Retirement finalisation cases are currently on hold due to a SCAPE (Superannuation Contributions Adjusted for Past Experience) factor change. The fund explicitly flags this as 'expected to impact performance in the coming months.' SCAPE changes directly drive pension valuations and employer contribution rates. The paper does not quantify the scale of the performance impact or the contribution rate effect.
findings.matters: As an employer in the scheme, Wolverhampton's contributions are set by SCAPE and fund valuations. A change that degrades casework performance may indicate a broader revaluation cycle affecting the council's employer contribution liability and future budget.
findings.figures: Currently 'a number of cases' on hold; normally over 96% of retirement finalisation cases completed within two weeks
findings.quote: A number of cases are currently on hold due to the SCAPE factor change, which is expected to impact performance in the coming months.

findings.headline: WMTL scheme transitioning to 0% equities and 55% liability-driven investment by July 2027, from 17% equities and 26% LDI
findings.detail: The West Midlands Travel Limited (WMTL) admitted body scheme is transitioning from a balanced allocation (17% listed equities, 21% multi-asset credit, 26% LDI) to a purely defensive strategy (0% equities, 0% multi-asset credit, 55% LDI) effective 1 July 2027. This eliminates all growth assets in favour of liabilities hedging. The transition is described as driven by the pace of Private Debt commitment drawdowns, but the completed allocation represents a fundamental shift in investment posture.
findings.matters: Moving to zero equity exposure and maximum liability hedging may indicate either a scheme surplus being locked in or a deficit requiring conservative positioning, either way signalling a material change in the sponsor's or administrator's risk assessment of this former Wolverhampton-related scheme.
findings.figures: WMTL listed equities moving from 17% current to 0% by July 2027; LDI rising from 26% to 55%; multi-asset credit falling from 21% to 0%; private debt holdings (£49m) increasing as growth assets are withdrawn
findings.quote: WMTL is in the process of transitioning its allocation towards its final target allocation as commitments to Private Debt are drawn down. Interim targets have been put in place predicated on the expected pace of drawdown.

findings.headline: Infrastructure assets have experienced write-downs on legacy transport investments due to refinancing challenges
findings.detail: The Infrastructure portfolio has incurred actual impairments on historical transport sector assets facing refinancing difficulties. The portfolio generated 6.4% returns over one year but has been materially impacted by these write-downs over longer periods, contributing to underperformance of 1.9% per annum against its benchmark over 5 years.
findings.matters: Write-downs represent actual losses on fund investments and signal either poor past investment decision-making or deteriorating conditions in the transport infrastructure sector, both of which raise questions about fund governance and asset quality that lenders use to assess council financial stewardship.
findings.figures: Infrastructure portfolio 6.4% over 1 year but underperformed by 1.9% per annum over 5 years due to write-downs
findings.quote: Long-term performance has been subdued by write-downs on legacy transport assets linked to refinancing challenges, as well as the concentrated nature of the portfolio in its early years.
